writeup: TIC 96680649 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 8.792365 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 3.49% dimming, while a secondary eclipse was not detected. The transit signal achieves a detection significance of 957.8 in the Box Least Squares search, and pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 23.2 and a centroid offset of 11.1 arcseconds from the target location. The candidate does not appear in six checked variable-star catalogs. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths - a pattern suggesting the true orbital period is double the initial detection, which is why the corrected period of 8.792365 days is reported here. The machine-learning screening score of 0.17 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real target rather than an artifact.
